live_handoff: SESSION 2026-07-26 #9: FOREST-CARRIERS S6 COMPLETE + RELEASED v0.51.0 (develop; master stays v0.48.0) — madc.ini. THE CARRIERS TRACK IS DONE (S1-S6). WHAT: madc optionally reads one madc.ini, and settings resolve CLI > environment > madc.ini > baked defaults — the rule the S3 discovery chain had reserved its last arm for. Keys: std (default dialect) / forest (a frozen-forest container = discovery ARM 5, the LAST arm) / include (repeatable, searched after every -I) / cpu-limit / mem-limit. Lookup ./madc.ini -> $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/madc/madc.ini (or ~/.config/madc/madc.ini) -> <sysconfdir>/madc.ini, and the FIRST EXISTING FILE WINS OUTRIGHT — configs are NEVER merged, because a merged chain makes 'why is this setting on?' unanswerable. Relative paths resolve against the config FILE's own directory (a system-wide /etc/madc.ini naming `forest = groves.msnap` means the file BESIDE IT, not something in whatever directory madc was started in); a leading ~/ expands. PRECEDENCE IS ENFORCED IN ONE VISIBLE PLACE (main(), after the argument loop), not spread across consumers: a --std= on the CLI wins via cli_set_std; -I dirs are already ahead of the ini's include dirs because the loop ran first (gcc searches configured dirs last); the environment wins by being read at each USE SITE before the ini value (MADC_FOREST is arm 4, the forest key is arm 5; install_resource_guards checks MADC_*_LIMIT before cpu-limit/mem-limit). STRICT, NOT TOLERANT: unknown key / foreign section / missing '=' / empty value / non-numeric limit = hard error naming file:line AND the accepted keys. A config file is the USER'S OWN FILE, so half-applying it is the silent degradation this project refuses — `mem-limit = 8G` says so instead of quietly arming an 8 MB guard. NO TOML DEPENDENCY (owner asked about toml11; answered and declined): the grammar is `key = value` for flat scalars, this code reads a file an attacker may influence in a sandboxed deployment so it is sized to be auditable line by line, and a template-heavy header library would raise the SELF-HOSTING bar for every file under src/. New flags --config=<file> (that file is the ENTIRE search and it MUST load — a named file that gets ignored is the same failure as a named forest container that gets ignored) and --no-config (skip the search; the two together are a contradiction and refuse). LAYERING (owner directive mid-slice: everything we build must be reusable by madc-dis and madc-dat — 3R credo): the reader is SCHEMA-BLIND. madc::cfg::config_file (include/madc_config_file.h, src/madc_config_file.cpp) owns the FORMAT — lookup chain, grammar, path resolution, strict diagnostics — and the consumer registers keys via accept_text / accept_text_list / accept_path / accept_path_list / accept_count / accept_flag. It is the SAME SPLIT madcdis/snapshot.h makes for the pool container: that container is CONTENT-blind with consumer-defined kinds, this reader is SCHEMA-blind with consumer-registered keys. Construct with the app name and everything app-specific follows: config_file("madcdat") reads madcdat.ini, searches madcdat's config dir, accepts a [madcdat] section, and its unknown-key diagnostic lists ITS keys — nothing in the reader knows a madc key spelling. src/madc_config.cpp is now ONLY madc's schema (five accept_* calls) + the CLI application. The header is deliberately PRIVATE/UNINSTALLED: include/madcdis/*.h is installed WHOLESALE by a wildcard, so putting it there would freeze a first-draft interface (API + ABI, libmadc.so is versioned) into shipped headers; in-tree consumers need no such promise — promote it to include/madcdis/config_file.h once a second consumer has exercised it. MY ORIGINAL MISTAKE, worth remembering: I reasoned 'a config file is a CLI-shape feature' (true — the POLICY of who may consult one is CLI-only) and collapsed that into 'so the reader is madc-CLI-private' (wrong — the MECHANISM is substrate). Two things fell out of WRITING THE SECOND CONSUMER'S TEST, which is exactly why that test exists: accept_text_list (I had registered madcdat's `peer` NAMES as a path list and the reader dutifully resolved alpha -> /tmp/alpha; a verbatim repeatable list is a real kind madc happens not to use) and a diagnostic-only `units` noun on accept_count (the move had silently cost mem-limit its 'of megabytes' hint, since the reader cannot know units). SANDBOX CONTRACT: libmadc NEVER reads a config file — one that can redirect where the compiler loads frozen state from is an attack surface for a fork+rlimit+seccomp host — so the CLI parses it and hands the forest path down through RegistrationPolicy::forest_config_path (on the POLICY, not a plain Program field, so --project TUs and runtime-eval children inherit it through the ONE propagation point, exactly like enable_forest_bind). Arm 5 sits INSIDE the enable_external_forest gate with the sidecar/env arms. configure --enable-config-file (default YES) gates madc's LOOKUP: OFF means the binary never searches for nor opens a madc.ini and --config= refuses naming the option. WORDING MATTERS HERE — it removes madc's LOOKUP, not 'the file-reading path entirely': the shared reader is ordinary in-tree code either way, and a parser nobody calls is not a call path. Do NOT gate the shared TU with the same define; that would make one flag change what madcdat can do (low-coupling violation). Each consumer gates its own lookup. ALSO IN THE SLICE: Program::forest_probed_arms() — ONE owner for the probed-arm list, so the loud fallback notice and the strict error can no longer drift from the real chain (and both name the madc.ini arm when one is configured). HERMETICITY: run_tests.sh passes --no-config on EVERY madc invocation (including the AOT compile legs, which deliberately take no $BACKEND_FLAG), and forest_pack.sh + forest_pack_darwin.sh do too — an ambient madc.ini carrying a std or include key would otherwise change the frozen corpus's PRODUCER CONFIG, after which every ordinary compile falls through the v27 dialect gate. A local /madc.ini is gitignored. BATCHED IN (owner directive: do NOT run a full suite for every tiny change — batch changes and test the GROUP): (a) the installed madcdis/snapshot.h did not compile downstream — it names PchCompression in its PUBLIC signatures but madc_pch.h was never installed; madc_pch.h (self-contained, standard includes only) now installs alongside, PROVEN BOTH WAYS by staging an install and compiling a TU that includes only <madcdis/snapshot.h>, then reproducing the original 'fatal error: madc_pch.h: No such file or directory' with the header removed. The DEEPER issue is a layering INVERSION — the substrate depends UPWARD on the PCH layer for the compression vocabulary, which should live in the substrate — recorded as task #22 (~15 files), NOT pretended fixed. (b) docs/build.md rewritten: it still listed asmjit as a build requirement with install-from-source steps and -lasmjit in the flag table, while the MIR fork, ./configure and its axes, the per-mode targets and the real object/test-binary paths were absent or wrong. TWO REAL BUGS THE VERIFICATION CAUGHT, both of the SILENT-NO-OP class: (1) config.mk.in was missing 'ENABLE_CONFIG_FILE = @ENABLE_CONFIG_FILE@', so --disable-config-file would have done NOTHING (the Makefile's ?= 1 default always won). Found only by exercising the configure path end-to-end instead of trusting the Makefile default — DO THIS for every new configure axis. (2) TRAP: the NAS carries a stale gitignored `configure`, and remote_build.sh sync PUSHES IT OVER the container's freshly generated one — so autoconf must run AFTER the last sync, or the substitution silently does not happen while ./configure --help still shows the new option. I pulled the regenerated configure back to the NAS so it does not recur. TESTING DISCIPLINE (owner directive 2026-07-26, now the rule): scope test runs by BLAST RADIUS — full battery only when a change touches shared codegen/runtime/emit, the forest container format, the product build shape, or the test harness itself; everything else gets the build plus the gates and unit tests covering the changed surface; a GROUP of changes gets one fulltest before the release commit. Do not run the whole battery for every teeny change. VALIDATION OF RECORD: fulltest 756/0/0/9 with forest_config_gate: OK (grouped run, on the final content); test_config_file 19 cases / 86 assertions; --exe 740/0 and packed arbiter 756/0/0/9 measured at feature commit 3edccef2 (attributed, not reclaimed — the re-cut after it cannot reach those lanes); make release packed 240 units + ledger (2 modules / 22 symbols / 3175 bytes) and the packed binary honours ./madc.ini and --no-config. NEXT: task #4 — fork MH_OBJECT .o flavor + merge read-back, which unblocks -static-libmadc in the .o LINK lane (an S5 stated boundary: the ledger merges into a compile CONTEXT, that lane merges native relocatables through MIR_object_read). Wants a FRESH context window for fork recon — compact before starting it. THEN the P2 darwin C++ lane (C-lane c++/v1 search order, libc++ parse burn-down, libc++ STD-ABI mangled-direct flavor; owner-confirmed to follow the carriers). SMALLER + well-scoped: DK_FPTR arena kind (darwin sig_t — fnptr typedefs still cannot ride the forest), __builtin_va_list as char* on arm64-darwin, prelude growth (sockets), task #22 (compression vocabulary into the substrate). NEEDS OWNER HARDWARE: the S5 Mac RUN leg (emit proven both arches; AMFI/run is not). DEFERRED: darwin dylib packaging shape, Windows/PE, the re-signer for already-signed Mach-O. STANDING: QNAP never builds/tests (container ssh -p 2299 dev@localhost does ALL; payloads need an explicit cd /workspace/madc; capture rc before piping); git commit -F; NEVER git add -A (owner WIP __c-tests-temp.*); cap every test run; one heavy container job (detached nohup + rc-file Monitor — and rm the rc file first, a stale one fires the monitor instantly); CLI flags BEFORE inputs; A QUESTION IS NEVER A DIRECTIVE; SDK NEVER committed/synced; configure is GENERATED/untracked (autoconf in the container AFTER the last sync); frozen forest = THE precompiled-header model BOTH platforms; embedded live-parse = fallback lane + freeze-time input ONLY. VLA sizeof in CONSTANT-required contexts (e.g. `int b[sizeof(vla_a)]`) still folds to 8 via the constant evaluate_type_query path (the expression-path fix doesn't reach it); alignof(vla_var) still reports pointer alignment 8 (gcc: element alignment). Same family, much rarer.

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.

MadArray/MadValue namespacing is an open API/ABI follow-up: moving the real C++ types to madc::array and madc::value would give PHP array helpers a normal namespace type surface, but compatibility aliases alone will not preserve old C++ mangled names.

Embedded <iostream> output remains partially staged: cout/cerr/clog still use header-defined stdio-backed ostream bodies. Follow-up is to replace that output surface with real libstdc++ declarations/operators, matching the std::cin direction; do not add stdio.h/FILE* stream bridges.
Real system-header PCH regeneration is deferred until PCH preserves include-guard/macro state; broad regenerated blobs currently duplicate transitive typedefs/declarations.

Explicit --std=c++ real iostream preprocessing reaches c2mir but fails on unresolved class/member aliases such as char_type, iter_type, iostate, __streambuf_type, __ostream_type, and __ios_type. Fix this generically through class/member alias resolution, not per-std shims.
